A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Magnetic Preference Optimization and contain complete, matching Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gemma-2B and Llama-3-8B alignment experiments, including safety evaluations, general-capability benchmarks, ablations and appendix baseline comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–3, the component ablations and the additional evaluations in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The MPO and MPO-RT objectives, policy updates, reference/opponent refresh procedures and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Revised theorem attributions do not modify the methods.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training data and evaluation coverage, including PKU-SafeRLHF, HH-Harmless, MixEval/MixEval-Hard, Open LLM Leaderboard v2, RewardBench and Kuhn Poker.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. This includes SFT controls and the PPO and Iterative DPO (Best-of-4 and Best-of-8) comparisons in Appendix D.1 and Figure 7.

E3.justification: The model configurations, sample budgets, three safety self-play rounds, four general-capability self-play rounds, evaluation metrics and testing procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

E4.justification: The no-self-play comparison, fixed-reference and clipping ablations in Section 4.1/Figure 5, and MPO-RT analyses in Appendix D.2 are retained unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The experimental text, tables and plots retain the same statistical reporting. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout, including Table 1's final costs of -11.38 and -3.86, Table 2's 79.5% final win rate, and Table 3's 33.95 final average. Appendix baseline and MPO-RT results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem F.1's proof changes the Lipschitz constant from L + L_B to L + αL_B, correctly accounting for G = F + α∇g. This is a localized mathematical correction; the theorem statement and convergence rate remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of last-iterate convergence to the original preference-game Nash equilibrium, computational/storage advantages and improved LLM alignment. No main contribution is added or withdrawn.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning opponent overfitting, periodic reference updates, uneven capability gains and MPO-RT's weaker performance are unchanged. No substantive applicability boundary or limitation is added.

D1.justification: Hyperparameter Tables 4, 6 and 7, hardware descriptions, implementation details, evaluation prompts and code/data access information are unchanged. Embedded external link targets also match.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly attributes Theorem 3.5 to Proposition D.7 and Lemmas E.2–E.3 to Lemmas D.3–D.4 of Sokota et al. (2022). Theorem 3.2 identifies its source directly instead of saying 'adapted from'. These clarify provenance without changing the bibliography or broader positioning.

P1.justification: The publication header replaces 'Preprint', and a Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence affiliation is added. Attribution wording receives local edits, while prose and section organization remain largely unchanged. New unresolved '?' references appear in Sections 1, 2.3 and 5.

P2.justification: Table 3 adds underlining to six per-task scores without changing their values. The affiliation and attribution additions cause small local layout shifts; figure content, captions and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the missing α factor in Theorem F.1 improves mathematical accuracy, while explicit source labels clarify the provenance of supporting theoretical results. These limited gains outweigh the minor presentation regression from three new unresolved references. The method, empirical evidence and central claims remain unchanged.
